text.p: Italian bond futures pared early losses due to the renewed strength in the lira and supported by comments from Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio on inflation and interest rates, dealers said.
Futures had opened lower on an overnight fall in U.S. T-bonds, the weakness of the lira on the back of a drifting dollar and as dealers moved to take profits.

The market took support after Fazio said Italian interest rate cuts could be speeded up if the 1997 budget was fully implemented and as he saw 1996 inflation at under four percent, but then profit takers moved in again deeped losses.
However, some dealers said the market was a little concerned after Fazio said the 1996 budget overshoot may be more than the government's 113 trillion lire target, by up to 20 trillion.
"We are taking a pause today along with the French and German markets after a long run of gains, but the overall mood is still positive," said one LIFFE trader.

Dealers added that after such a strong rise there was bound to be some profit taking especially after other markets showed some weakness and the Italian equity market continued to drag and had not shown the recent sparkling performance of BTPs.
